requirement:
The SDK's backend integration makes the rendered prefix available to its supported
prompt-caching mechanism. The prefix includes all context, including the
question, and precedes node contents. A cache hit is not guaranteed.
The prefix fingerprint follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.agent_context`.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.caching`. Each obligation maps to a marked test with assertions that enforce it. The only item with no test is the "cache hit is not guaranteed" sentence, which states no behaviour. **Obligations and the tests that cover them** 1. **The backend integration makes the rendered prefix available to the prompt-caching mechanism.** Both implementing agents pass the prefix as the provider's leading preamble, which is what a provider's cache checkpoints attach to. The implementations are `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[ToolAgent/Agent]` and `src/authoring/sdk.rs#impl[ReviewAgent

/Agent>]`. - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` asserts `requests[0].chat_history[0] == Message::system("Question é")`. The system message is exactly the prefix, including the non-ASCII text. - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version]` compares the whole provider request with the expected request. That request carries the system prompt as the preamble and the subject as the user message. 2. **The prefix includes all context, including the question.** - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[contexts_render_once_allow_non_send_values_and_hash_exact_prefix_text]` chains `.context(&context)` with a `(policy, question)` tuple. It asserts the delivered prefix is `"héllo\n\npolicy\n\nquestion"`. - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[string_and_str_contexts_deliver_identical_prefixes_and_fingerprints]` covers repeated `.context` calls, tuples, slices, `Vec`, and `String` versus `&str`. Each case asserts the exact prefix delivered to the agent. 3. **The prefix precedes node contents.** - In the `ToolAgent` test, the system message is `chat_history[0]`. The user message at `chat_history[1]` contains `formatted input: source`, the node contents. - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[string_and_str_contexts_deliver_identical_prefixes_and_fingerprints]` also shows node inputs delivered separately from the prefix. The prefix is unchanged with `contents_of_current_node`, `contents_of_successors`, and no inputs. 4. **The prefix fingerprint follows `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.agent_context`.** - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[prefix_hashes_match_known_utf8_sha256_without_normalization]` checks known SHA-256 values and the versioned scheme name `context-prefix-sha256-v1`. It also checks that `é` and `e\u{301}` differ and that `"a b"` and `"a b"` differ, so there is no normalisation. - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[contexts_render_once_allow_non_send_values_and_hash_exact_prefix_text]` asserts that each delivered fingerprint equals `context_fingerprint(prefix)`. It asserts that an empty context gives the empty prefix and the empty fingerprint. It asserts order sensitivity (`a\n\nb` differs from `b\n\na`) and that repetition is preserved in the rendered prefix. - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[string_and_str_contexts_deliver_identical_prefixes_and_fingerprints]` asserts that the fingerprint matches `context_fingerprint(text)` for every request, including requests that carry node inputs. 5. **A cache hit is not guaranteed.** This sentence states no behaviour, so nothing needs testing. **Out of scope** - The Bedrock cache-checkpoint placement in `providers.rs` is cited under `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`, which has its own tests. It is not an implementation site of this requirement. - The rendering rules for the context types belong to the cited `agent_context` requirement. Even so, the tests above check them as they apply to the prefix and fingerprint. I found no plausible requirement-violating behaviour that these tests would accept, and no marking gaps.

text: :::{req} judge.caching
The SDK's backend integration makes the rendered prefix available to its supported
prompt-caching mechanism. The prefix includes all context, including the
question, and precedes node contents. A cache hit is not guaranteed.
The prefix fingerprint follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.agent_context`.
:::{req} agent_context
Supplies reusable prompt text for an agent request. `contents` may borrow or own the string.
The SDK implements this trait for the following combinations:
| Value | Rendering |
| `String` | Use its text directly. |
| `str` | Use its text directly; `&str` works through the reference implementation. |
| `&C`, where `C: Context + ?Sized` | Forward to the referenced value. |
| `[C]` and `Vec<C>`, where `C: Context` | Render elements in order, separated by two newlines. An empty collection renders an empty string. |
| Heterogeneous tuples of 2 through 12 `Context` values | Render elements in order, separated by two newlines. |
Combinations can nest and preserve repeated elements. Each `.context(value)`
call obtains the text once and retains it for both the prefix and its hash,
without retaining a borrow of `value`. The value needs no `Hash`, `Serialize`,
`Send`, or `Sync` implementation. Repeated calls use the same two-newline
separator as combinations. No context calls give the empty prefix and the
same fingerprint as an explicitly empty rendered prefix.
The cache fingerprint hashes the exact UTF-8 prefix delivered to the agent,
using a versioned scheme. It preserves order and repetition and uses neither
object addresses nor type identities. It identifies this prefix, including the
question; node inputs, the result schema, and the rest of the request are outside
that fingerprint.
